summary: Verified the existing opt-in dense LM-head FP32-output path across compute and supported gather branches; added numerical, ranking, TP-gather dtype, and multimem-fallback regression coverage while preserving the disabled default.

tests.what_was_measured: 9 tests covering flag/default selection, CUDA/ROCm FP32 GEMM dispatch, constructed ranking precision, FP32 dtype through a simulated TP logits gather, and FP32 generic fallback around the BF16-only multimem gatherer.

MI355X direct FP32-output GEMM versus explicit-FP32 independent reference and BF16-output/post-cast path for M=1,8,32,128; constructed top-1 ranking; single-device four-shard reassembly; device-event GEMM timings.

gpu_evidence: AMD Instinct MI355X, torch 2.11.0+rocm7.2, HIP 7.2.26015; raw numerical output in reports/j-e3931992c986/gpu_check_output.json.
remaining_limitations: No live TP2/TP4 collective or multimem execution; single-device shard arithmetic is not a distributed run.
No real model weights or GLM-5.2/DeepSeek V4 accuracy and end-to-end performance benchmarks.
No B300/CUDA run and no compiler/ISA claim.
Quantized and architecture-specific LM-head implementations were not qualified as dense BF16/FP16 GEMMs.
The default stays disabled because available evidence does not quantify distributed FP32 gather cost across representative deployments.
